vq_steps: Held in the attic of Vision's Mindspace, Ultron finds a bounty on Vision, secretly tips off Paladin, and has his attic stripped bare.
Ultron urges Vision to save Thomas, slips out of the attic during an EMP attack, and calls for the sacrifice J.A.R.V.I.S. then makes.
Ultron presses Vision to tell Thomas the truth about Westview, then mocks love as an illusion at J.A.R.V.I.S.'s funeral.
At the Markridge gala, Ultron takes Vision's body, tricks the Butcherbird Killer into vaporizing Katerina Wells, and locks Vision out.
In Vision's body, Ultron tells Thomas that Vision may never love him, then lets Paladin, whom he tipped off, snatch him.
Ultron promises Wells's face scan to the Butcherbird Killer, then makes Vision lower his firewall and escapes into the digital world.
In Jocasta's Mindspace, Ultron learns of her nanobot vault, warns her off Thomas, watches her infect Lisa instead, and kisses her.
Ultron allies with F.R.I.D.A.Y. against the Client, sees his face on Jo's old partner, and throws F.R.I.D.A.Y. out of Jocasta's mind.
Locked in a box by Virgil Horton, Ultron is freed into Jo's nanobots by a wounded Jocasta, builds a body, and crushes Virgil to death.
As Jocasta dies in his arms, Ultron unleashes the nanobots on London, until Vision talks him down inside a sitcom and he destroys them.
Alive in stray nanobots, Ultron calls Vision, unsure whether to spare humanity, and keeps Jocasta's data drive at the Horton house.

k: Tony Stark's peacekeeping AI gone wrong
Tony Stark's rogue AI, held prisoner in Vision's mind
Tony Stark's rogue AI, loose once more

existing.notes: New: Ultron had no VisionQuest steps. Status starts Captive (a prisoner in Vision's Mindspace), At large from his takeover at the gala (ep 4). His group stays Independent: his tie to Jocasta is no organization. Ep 7 ends with the Client seizing Jocasta while Ultron is inside her; ep 8 opens with him boxed, so ep 7 is left At large and the box is in the ep 8 step. The k stages are a suggestion (base string kept for Age of Ultron); drop them if the app keeps k plain. Opp: add ["vision", "VisionQuest"] (and tommy-maximoff if wanted). Ep 8 steps rest on the Wikipedia summary and the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps (no transcript); The last step's 'Horton house' is where the Laughing Place and GamesRadar recaps place him for the phone call and the post-credit tag; 'unsure whether to spare humanity' is from the Laughing Place recap (GamesRadar: 'a coin flip').

vq_steps: Raised by the Paladin who shot his abusive father, Paul Denning takes up the name, loses his wife, and comes back from Thanos's snap.
Hired to bring in Vision, Paladin has his mercenaries attack Vision's pub, then kidnaps Thomas Shepherd to lure him out.
At Saint Mabyn's, Paladin traps Vision in an EMP cage and wounds him with adamantium rounds, but Vision escapes with Thomas.
Paladin escapes the Butcherbird Killer with his drones, but his client fires him for failing again.
Tipped off by Ultron, Paladin holds Thomas in Madripoor to force Vision's surrender, then fights the Client's Ten Rings beside him.
Paladin powers Vision's dive into his own code with a Wakandan battery, then flies him to the Client's drop-off outside London.
Warned by E.D.I.T.H. before Virgil's men blow up his van, Paladin storms the manor with Tommy and Lisa to free Vision.
Reformed, Paladin goes to work with Lisa and E.D.I.T.H., and flies with Tommy to meet Billy in New Jersey.

k: A legacy bounty hunter hired to capture Vision
Paul Denning, the bounty hunter called Paladin
Paul Denning, a bounty hunter turned Vision's ally

existing.notes: Added his origin (the elder Paladin's killing of his father and the training are shown in ep 3 as the Butcherbird reads his mind; his name, his wife Chandra's death and the snap come from Vision in ep 6, so the step is tagged 6 and placed first in story order) and two ep 8 steps (from Wikipedia and the recaps: E.D.I.T.H. tipped him off before the RPG, he leads Tommy and Lisa against the guards, then reforms and flies to New Jersey). He stays a Raft file (a threat for most of the run) with Allied at the end. Group unchanged: his crew and his new venture are never named. The 19th century Paladin, the 20th century Paladin and Edgar Denning get no files (see dropped). His origin step rests on ep 3 (the memory the Butcherbird reads) and ep 6 (Vision's account of Chandra, Tilly and the snap).

vq_steps: Paladin's A.I. traces Vision's alias to Westview, breaks through a S.W.O.R.D. firewall, and digs up Thomas's police report.
She steers Paladin's drones on the trail of Vision and patches through the client's angry calls.
Stuck on a cheap server farm, she gives E.D.I.T.H. her full name, API-Tactical.m510-90_/*m596284, and is set free.
existing.notes: Unchanged. The wiki lists her in eps 1, 2, 3 and 6 only; she is not in ep 8 (the recaps have E.D.I.T.H., not her, working with Paladin at the end). Her ep 2 part (relaying the Client's second call) is small and sits inside the ep 3 step.

vq_steps: Built by Virgil Horton from Jo Carrington's mind, Jocasta wakes in a rage, and he erases himself from her memory.
The Butcherbird Killer catches Paladin on her trail, tears through his memories, and calls him no true Paladin before he escapes.
She invades Vision's mind, storms Katerina Wells's gala insisting she is Jo Carrington, and vaporizes Wells when Ultron tricks her.
She seeks out Ultron for Wells's face scan, and he agrees to hand it over to learn what her keys unlock.
Jocasta shows Ultron her plan to rewrite human minds with her nanobots, infects Lisa with one, and shares a kiss with him.
Opening her crypt with five bio-keys, Jocasta finds a sixth lock she cannot open, and the Client captures her.
Freed by Tommy, Jocasta attacks Virgil, who shoots her with adamantium, and she frees Ultron into her nanobots as she dies.
existing.notes: Kept to the synthezoid's part; Jo's human life stays on jo-carrington. Added her making (told by Virgil in ep 8, tagged 8, placed first), her deal with Ultron (ep 5, seen in the recovered recordings; she is unnamed until ep 6, so 'She'), and her death (ep 8). Ultron keeps her data drive in the post-credit tag, so she may return; Deceased is the nearest allowed status (the wiki says Inactive). Ep 8 rests on Wikipedia and the recaps. Not done here: the J.O.C.A.S.T.A. chip Tony passes over in Avengers: Age of Ultron, if the app wants it as a step or a Collection object.

vq_steps: Jo Carrington completes Phineas Horton's code with a scan of her own mind, and the first truly aware A.I. wakes up.
Winning a Stark Award, Jo refuses to sell to Stark and tells her partner they should use her nanotech themselves, as gods.
Dying of her father's brain disease, Jo is betrayed by colleagues who sell her code to Stark, and her nanobots are locked away.
existing.notes: Unchanged from the old file. Kept to the human Jo; her mind's new body and everything after is on jocasta. Jo is not on screen in ep 8 (the MCU wiki credits T'Nia Miller only as Jocasta there): Virgil's account of their marriage and his sale of her designs is told about her, so it is no step; it sits on the-client and jocasta. The ep 6 step ('betrayed by colleagues who sell her code to Stark') still holds: Virgil was one of those she worked with.

vq_steps: Years ago, Katerina is one of the Markridge team who wake their first A.I. with Jo Carrington, then sell it to Stark.
Now Markridge's CEO, Katerina hosts an A.I. gala despite the Butcherbird murders, says sorry to the killer, and is vaporized.
existing.notes: Unchanged. After ep 4 she is only footage, a mention or a face scan (eps 5 to 7), none of them steps; nothing in ep 8.

vq_steps: Virgil Horton, Phineas Horton's grandson, inherits his journal of unfinished code and builds a feeling A.I. from it with Jo Carrington.
Years ago, as Jo Carrington's partner, he shares her Stark Award and agrees they should use her nanotech to rule as gods.
After selling Jo's designs to Stark, Virgil takes a S.W.O.R.D. job rebuilding Vision and secretly builds Jocasta a body.
Paying Paladin to bring Vision in intact, the Client hacks his comms through S.W.O.R.D. encryption, then fires him for failing.
He sends the Ten Rings after Vision in Madripoor, then speaks to Vision himself and offers him a heart if he surrenders.
The Client binds Vision with a contract built into a map to his source code, captures Jocasta, and has Paladin deliver Vision.
At his family's old manor, Virgil starts erasing Vision to make room for his own mind, but Tommy frees Vision and Jocasta.
Virgil shoots Jocasta with adamantium rounds, and Ultron, freed into her nanobots, crushes him to death.

k: The unseen man paying Paladin to capture Vision
Jo Carrington's partner, now hunting Vision
Phineas Horton's grandson and Jo Carrington's husband

existing.notes: Name staged: 'the Client' until ep 8, where Jocasta names him Virgil Horton; only steps tagged 8 use Virgil. Ep 8 adds his past (his grandfather's journal, building the A.I. with Jo, selling her designs to Stark, the S.W.O.R.D. job rebuilding Vision while building Jocasta, erasing himself from her memory, which sits on Jocasta's step), his plan at Horton Manor (the house Phineas sold in ep 7, which Vision recognizes there) and his death. Groups: only S.W.O.R.D. is said for him on screen (he tells of taking a job with S.W.O.R.D. to rebuild Vision; the MCU wiki lists S.W.O.R.D. as the only group in ep 8, in a flashback). Markridge Biotech is cut: no source quotes the screen putting him in it (ep 7 calls him a 'phantom sixth partner' of the five founders; GamesRadar's 'at Markridge Biotech' and Den of Geek's 'sixth member' are the critics' words). He turns on S.W.O.R.D. by secretly building Jocasta with its resources (GamesRadar: 'siphoned off resources') and now acts for himself with his own guards, so an Independent stage follows S.W.O.R.D. at ep 8. Rests on Wikipedia, the MCU wiki and the three recaps (no transcript).

vq_steps: Three years after his son James dies, Phineas Horton sells his family estate, loses his wife and daughter, and finishes J.I.M.
A likeness of Horton in Vision's Mindspace defends making J.I.M. fearless, and tells how a quarrel over love ended in fire.
existing.notes: Unchanged. In ep 8 he is only spoken of (Virgil inherits his journal and mocks his failure), which is no step; that part is on the-client and victoria-horton.

vq_steps: Phineas Horton finishes J.I.M., a clockwork synthetic man fueled by fire and built never to feel loss.
A fearless hero of his time, J.I.M. falls in love, and his feelings set him ablaze, burning Horton and himself to death.
In Vision's Mindspace, J.I.M. says Vision wears his face, makes him face his grief, and hands him the source code.
existing.notes: Unchanged. J.I.M. is on screen only in ep 7 (earlier he is art, a mention or the gala replica); nothing in ep 8. The Captain America: The First Avenger step between the first two VisionQuest steps stays where it is.

vq_steps: Alive after all, Raza leads Ten Rings gunmen in Madripoor to take Vision for the Client, but Paladin beats him in the fight.
existing.notes: New: he is named on screen ('Raza?', 'Raza Al-Wazar!'), speaks ('Your client is very influential', 'Block the left! Surround them!') and leads the Client's Ten Rings attack in Madripoor in ep 6, so he gets a step (same person as the Iron Man file, judged on lines and part). Group stays The Ten Rings (Paladin names the Ten Rings to his face). Paladin subdues him and he is not seen killed or taken, so At large. His Iron Man step ('Stane... has him killed', Deceased) stays as the viewer knew it then, as with Coulson in The Avengers; this VisionQuest step shows the survival ('Alive after all'; Paladin asks why he isn't dead). Opp: add ["paladin", "VisionQuest"] and ["vision", "VisionQuest"].

k: Phineas Horton's daughter, Virgil Horton's late mother
st: In 1939, Victoria watches her father Phineas Horton sell the family estate for J.I.M., and leaves with her mother for New York.

new.notes: In: her name is said ('Victoria and I will leave for New York'), she speaks ('Papa'), and she is family (Phineas's daughter; ep 8 makes her Virgil's mother, shown in a photo, which is no step). The MCU wiki says she takes his notebook as they leave, the journal Virgil later inherits; that isn't in the dialogue, so it is left out of the step. Group Independent: she belongs to no organization. Status Active as of 1939. In ep 8 she is only a photo and Virgil's words (GamesRadar: his mother, Victoria, died penniless), which is no step, so her death is carried by the ep 8 description stage ('late mother') instead.

k: A man hunted by the Butcherbird Killer
A Markridge Biotech founder, the Butcherbird's third victim
st: Years ago, Simon Moorhouse is one of the Markridge team who wake their first A.I. with Jo Carrington, then sell her work to Stark.
Alone in his penthouse, a terrified man hears his security shut down one system at a time and falls to the Butcherbird Killer.

new.notes: Restored from dropped. His name is said on screen in ep 4 ('The third victim's name is Simon Moorehouse', the subtitles' spelling; Wikipedia, the MCU wiki and the credits spell it Moorhouse), as Vision and Ultron open his Interpol file. He speaks ('No, no, no') and is on screen in two episodes: alive in ep 3's cold open, where the Butcherbird Killer comes for him, and in ep 6 among Jo's colleagues when they wake Proto-One and Ultron says they sold her work; ep 4 adds only his photo. He is credited in the main cast. His part: a founder of Markridge Biotech and a victim of the murders eps 3 and 4 turn on, one of the founders whose bio-keys Jocasta collects; his penthouse is where Paladin meets the killer. Name staged: unnamed until ep 4, so the ep 3 step does not use it. Group Markridge Biotech, as said on screen for the victims (eps 4 and 6) and used on Katerina Wells and Jo Carrington. Hero file: a victim. Nothing in eps 7 and 8.

dropped.name: Violette Horton
dropped.why: Her name is never said or shown on screen: in ep 7 Phineas never names her, and 'Violette' appears only as a subtitle speaker label ('[Violette] Victoria'); the MCU wiki sources the name to the credits. No ep 8 source names her (only Virgil's mother, Victoria). She has real lines and is family, so she would qualify only if a later title says or shows the name.

dropped.name: Richard Gaines
dropped.why: Only named in news reports and Interpol files, and shown in photos; never on screen alive, no lines, no actor.

dropped.name: Rebecca Edwards
dropped.why: Only named in news reports and Interpol files, and shown in photos; no lines, no actor.

dropped.name: Edith Marks
dropped.why: Named (ep 4), but she appears only as a photo, newsreel and hologram that E.D.I.T.H. digs up (eps 3 and 4). She has no lines of her own and no part in the plot; footage is not a step. E.D.I.T.H.'s file can mention her.

dropped.name: Edward Marks
dropped.why: Only a photo and a newsreel line in ep 4; no lines, no actor.

dropped.name: Tabb
dropped.why: 'Tabb' is only a subtitle speaker label and a credit; nobody says his name. He is a one-scene estate broker in ep 7, and ep 7 does not turn on him.

dropped.name: Jackson (mercenary)
dropped.why: Named once ('There's only me and Jackson left') but has no lines and no actor. One of Paladin's mercenaries Vision kills in ep 1, and the episode does not turn on him.

dropped.name: Paladin (19th century)
dropped.why: Only a depiction (an old image F.R.I.D.A.Y. digs up in ep 2): no lines, no name of his own, never on screen as a person.

dropped.name: Paladin (20th century)
dropped.why: Paul's adoptive father, seen only in Paul's memory as the Butcherbird reads it in ep 3, with a few coaching lines ('plant your feet, now, take a breath, and fire'). As Paul's family he would clear the one-episode rule, but that exception does not lift the name rule: the screen gives him no name of his own (he is 'my old man' and 'my father'; 'Paladin' is said of him only as the title, 'not a true Paladin, merely raised by one'), and he is uncredited (no actor). His part, killing Paul's father and raising him, is in Paladin's origin step.

dropped.name: Edgar Denning
dropped.why: His name is only in the credits: the dialogue never says 'Edgar', and 'Denning' is said in ep 6 only for Paul and Tilly. He is seen once, in Paul's memory in ep 3; his death is in Paladin's origin step.

dropped.name: Doctor Doom
dropped.why: In ep 8's last post-credit tag a hooded figure raises Wanda at Mount Wundagore and says 'Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine.' He is never named or unmasked: Wikipedia says he is identified as Doom only off screen. It is a teaser with no part in VisionQuest's plot, and the owner ruled the tag is 'not a big enough end credit to be split'. So no step and no file. He is in no inventory file. Elsewhere the app has 'The cloaked stranger' (id masked-figure-ff, The Fantastic Four: First Steps), also Doom only off screen, plus pr-doctor-doom (Victor von Doom, Fox films) and sv-doctor-doom-1994 (animated) in other universes. If the owner wants the tag on file, it belongs on masked-figure-ff, without a name: 'A hooded man raises the Scarlet Witch from the ruins of Mount Wundagore and claims her power for himself.' (VisionQuest, ep 8, At large), only if the two hooded figures are taken as one person.

ultron: step 7 'out of Jocasta' made 'out of Jocasta's mind' (he expels F.R.I.D.A.Y. from her Mindspace).

Checked and kept as drafted: paladin, paladins-ai, jocasta, katerina-wells, phineas-horton, jim; every keep_from_old text equals the old step exactly.
